title: ODRS Attestation
description: A party's verified claims about another ODRS object — most commonly a buyer's or third party's acceptance verdicts on a delivered DATASET against a request's acceptance criteria. An attestation says WHO checked WHAT, HOW, and what they found. ODRS deliberately mandates no PKI: the optional signature block carries one if the parties use one, and platform/registry context otherwise establishes authorship.

subject.description: The object the claims are about. REQUIRED. When the subject is a dataset, the checksum SHOULD be repeated here so the attestation binds to one exact artifact even if the dataset manifest later changes.

attestor.description: Who makes these claims, and their relationship to the transaction — a buyer's acceptance, a supplier's self-declaration, and an independent audit carry different weight, and the role field makes that difference machine-readable. REQUIRED.

claims.description: The verified statements. REQUIRED, at least one. Each claim carries its own measurement description — an unverifiable claim is not an attestation, it is an opinion.

property.description: What is being attested: a well-known metric (sync_error_ms, task_success_rate, ...), a criterion id from the request's acceptance block, or a named property ('consent_artifacts_complete', 'checksum_matches').

criterion_id.description: The acceptance.criteria[].id in the referenced request this verdict answers, when applicable.

verdict.description: 'measured' = a value is reported without a pass/fail threshold; 'inconclusive' = the check was attempted but could not be completed (say why in measurement).

value.description: The measured value, when there is one.

threshold.description: The threshold applied, when verdict is pass/fail.

measurement.description: How this was checked: method, tooling, population, sample size. REQUIRED — same discipline as acceptance criteria.

scope.description: What portion of the subject the claims cover.

outcome.description: The attestor's overall disposition, when the attestation is an acceptance decision. 'informational' for third-party measurements that carry no accept/reject authority.

signature.description: Optional cryptographic signature over the canonical JSON of this document minus this block. ODRS mandates no PKI; if the parties use one, this is where it goes.
